terms.gloss: extortion (by an official); literally “money to be recovered”
evidence: Lewis & Short s.v. repetō: money extorted by a provincial governor, and that is to be restored
Cic. Rab. Post. 4.9: accūsāre dē pecūniīs repetundīs (Lewis & Short s.v. repetō)
terms.comment: The Roman charge of extortion was named from the money the victims sued to recover: dē pecūniīs repetundīs, or simply repetundārum.
Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase. Classical exāctiō is the demanding of payment.

sources: Lewis & Short: repeto · Lewis & Short: exactio
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 195, 312.
